216177.overview:
Laser Defense is a 1 - 2 player arcade game for the TRS-80.

The player controls a series of satellite-based laser defense platforms, and must stop an incursion of Eastern European nuclear weapons. Played on two maps, the player freely switches between an American and European map. On the map of America, the player must move a cross-hair to target incoming intercontinental ballistic missiles to blow them up before they reach and destroy American cities. If all American cities are lost, it's game over. On the European map, the player must target enemy missile sites and other offensive weapons. If the player destroys all enemy missile sites, they advance to the next level. The enemy nation will also create an Eradicator, which can shoot down the laser defense system. If this is allowed to power up, it's game over. Current Eradicator power and remaining laser defense power are displayed on the bottom of the screen. 

The game is essentially a derivative of Missile Command.

317405.overview: Laser Ball is similar to Pac-Man but has two major differences from the Namco game. For starters, the maze is empty when the game starts and instead of eating all the dots the objective is to drop dots so that the whole maze is completely covered by them. The other big difference is how the power pills (here called stimulators) work. Like in Pac-Man they allow the player (the laser ball) to go after the enemies (which are called destructoids) but instead of eating them it shoots lasers at them. Lasers are only available for a short while but there is no limit on how many shots can be made within that time. If the laser ball is touched by a destructoid during this time, the destructoid will piggyback on the ball and destroy it when the charge ends. To shake it off, the player has to turn a three- or four way intersection at a 90 degree angle.

353855.overview: Laser Blazer is a basic shooting game with a first-person view. You use the arrow keys to move the targeting sights around and then fire when ready. You can also activate shields if needed. The enemies look like a mixture of Tie Fighters from Star Wars, Klingon cruisers from Star Trek, and basic flying saucers.

353856.overview:
After your death in hospital, you have been wrongly sent down to Hell from the gates of Heaven where you find Lucifer himself has his own problems. He has discovered that Adolf Hitler is attempting to raise an army including Mussolini and Reverend Jim, to overthrow Lucifer and take over Hell. He has tasked you to stop Hitler in his power struggle and as a reward you can return back up to Heaven.

Lucifer's Realm is a graphic text adventure where you see pictures for each location while text below describes what you can see in the location. You type commands with the keyboard to control your hero and interact with various locations.

353893.overview:
Lunar Lander is one of many variants on a moon landing theme.

The player controls a small lunar modules, whose goal is to land on one of the few safe flat plains on the moon's surface. The player has limited fuel, and receives points for each successful landing they make. The player controls vertical and horizontal thrust, with gravity continuously pulling the vessel downward. The player is awarded points based upon the difficulty of each landing site. If the player makes contact with the ground too fast or on uneven terrain, their lander is lost.

In the TRS-80 version, the screen zooms in as the player closely approaches the ground. The player starts with 5000 fuel, and must make as many landings that they can with this. In the Atari version, the screen is fixed, and the player has a total of 5 landing attempts to maximize score.

354086.overview:
Leaper is Frogger clone for the TRS-80.

The player controls a frog, who must cross a busy highway while avoiding cars and trucks. They must then cross a raging river by jumping across logs and lilypads. The goal is to place all frogs within their home at the top of the screen, at which point the player progresses to a more difficult challenge. The player starts with three frogs, and if all are lost, it's game over.

417585.overview: Number two in the "Interactive Fiction" series.

417605.overview:
Labyrinth is a first-person adventure game for multiple systems.

You have been deposited in a labyrinth haunted by an evil Minotaur, armed only with a single torch. The player must navigate from a first-person perspective the twisting passageways of the labyrinth, looking for clues and items to defeat their foe. The player has a limited number of turns as they must find more torches and food, or else die of starvation or be killed by the Minotaur in the darkness. The player must solve inventory-based problems, and deal with foes including a gnome, a cave bear, a witch, and an ugly little man. Eventually, the player must lure the Minotaur into the torchlight and slay it with a special weapon.

417619.overview:
The first clue as to the unconventional nature of this text adventure is the scant description within the game manual. Unlike most games of its era, Lords of Karma doesn't rely on a written narrative peppered with enticing illustrations to prepare and color the player's experience. Even Lords of Karma's plot is to be discovered in-game, just like the vistas and scents of its magical world. There is treasure, of course, and deadly foes, but what to do with the spoils of adventure? You only know that you quest for "karma points" to take to heaven, and that you begin in the central square of the mythical city of Golconda.

The standard abbreviations and two-word commands move you through this text-only, turn-based adventure, but don't stand there gawking. While looking twice can reveal something missed the first time, it will also put you in the maw of a hungry crocodile. Happily, rebirth is just around the corner. Dying doesn't end your game -- the karmic wheel keeps turning. It simply strips you of your worldly goods and puts you on a mountaintop. The map is fixed, and the karma points are yours to keep, so progress belongs to the persistent (and those who find the in-game hint book).

417620.overview:
Life Two are games based upon John Conway's Game of Life

Contains a TRS-80 implementation of the Game of Life.

Any live cell with fewer than two live neighbours dies, as if caused by under-population.
Any live cell with two or three live neighbours lives on to the next generation.
Any live cell with more than three live neighbours dies, as if by overcrowding.
Any dead cell with exactly three live neighbours becomes a live cell, as if by reproduction.
Also contains a competitive form called The Battle of Life, where 2 - 4 players place 1 - 5 animated characters in a 10 x 5 board. Every 5 generations, the remaining players can place two more lifeforms. Gameplay continues until there is only a single player remaining.

417622.overview:
This is a compilation release of the "Rider Fantasy Creations" series.

Lost Dutchman's Gold - is a text based adventure game. Your goal in the game is to find the legendary lost Dutchman's gold. You begin the game in a miner's shack; searching about, you find a map which seems to indicate where the lost gold is located. Now you'll set out on a dangerous quest through deserts, mountains, and even ghost towns in order to locate the mine where the gold is buried. The ghost of Back-Pack Sam (better known as the computer) will guide you on your quest by providing descriptions and clues. You get around and interact with the game by entering two word commands. Good luck!

Spider Mountain Adventure - you are a knight stationed at the base of Spider Mountain, and your goal is gather the four treasures hidden beneath the tavern of an abandoned village. As the player explores the surface, they can encounter orcs, but they leave the player alone if unprovoked. The player must discover how to explore beneath the tavern, and there must locate a gold ring, mithril arming doublets, a sack of gold ducats, and a jewel. Upon locating these four items, they player must return them to the tavern, receiving their final score if all items are dropped.

462060.overview:
Lost Ship Adventure is a text adventure game for the TRS-80.

Lazily floating in the balmy waters of the South Seas is a mystery ship. She's rigged and ready for a voyage to an unknown destination.

The player finds themselves aboard the lost pirate ship. They must learn how to navigate the ship, which takes them to a mysterious treasure island. There, they must find 4 lost treasures, and return them to the ship's hold. All commands are via VERB NOUN entry, and there is a save/restore game option.

462204.overview:
Liberator is a 1-player arcade game for the TRS-80.

The player must rescue humans from the alien menace by navigating a number of difficult platforms. Plays similar to the arcade game Donkey Kong, where on many levels the player must jump over barrels thrown from the alien atop the screen to reach the human stranded nearby. Other levels require the player to stand on a number of platforms while avoiding alien slimes. The player starts with 5 lives, and loses these from touching alien creatures, barrels, or falling from great height.
